key_insight: This study compares three ways to evaluate enterprise analytics agents: judging execution traces, judging text outputs with red-teaming, and applying deterministic rules. The provided abstract is truncated, so it does not establish which approach performs best.
problem_solved: How to reliably detect failures in enterprise analytics agents whose workflows involve multiple tools, while assessing evaluation stability, failure detection, and discovery.
method: Conduct a three-phase comparison of three distinct evaluation paradigms in a controlled research setting.
Apply trace-based LLM judging, text-only LLM judging with red-teaming, and deterministic heuristics to two analytics agents.
Use frozen execution traces to compare evaluators on fixed agent behavior.
impact: The comparison can help practitioners choose evaluation approaches for complex enterprise agents. Frozen traces allow evaluator differences to be examined without changes in agent execution confounding the comparison.
visual_elements: Three-column comparison showing the inputs and mechanisms of each evaluation paradigm.
Workflow diagram connecting two analytics agents, frozen execution traces, and three evaluators.
Three evaluation lenses labeled stability, failure detection, and failure discovery.
Multi-tool workflow illustration highlighting potential failure points.
paper_title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
paper_authors: Howard Zhang, Chuck Arvin, Logan Brown, Mihir Bhatia, Neelu Choudhary
